title: distlock users file
description: Credentials for clients of the distlock server. A user's client_id is the application name that appears on every session it opens. Not expressible in this schema but enforced by the server at load time: client_id values must be unique (case-sensitive), and the file should not be readable by group or others.

$schema.description: Editor hint only; ignored by the server.

description.description: Free-form note for humans; ignored by the server.

client_id.description: Application name and login name. Many processes may share one client_id; each opens its own session.

password_hash.description: bcrypt hash for password logins (auth mode 1), cost 10-31 (12 recommended). Generate with scripts/hash-password.sh. Never store a plaintext password here. Optional when the user has public_keys.

enabled.description: false rejects new logins for this client_id without deleting the entry.

description.description: Free-form note for humans (owner, purpose); ignored by the server.

public_keys.description: Ed25519 public keys for key logins (auth mode 2). Make a pair with `python -m distlock.keys`: the public half goes here, the private half stays with the client. A user may have a password hash, public keys, or both.

key.description: The 32-byte public key in base64 (standard or URL-safe, with or without padding): 43 characters unpadded.

identifier.description: A name for people (laptop, ci-2025). Written to the server log when the key logs someone in.

issuer.description: Who vouched for the key. Metadata only; never read by the server.

expiry.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with an offset, e.g. 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z. From then on the key no longer logs anyone in. Sessions already open are not affected.
